verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes an implementation-relevant review-artifact requirement: images must be directly viewable or delivered as JPG or PNG.
First concrete failure: the client could not open the uploaded review image on a Mac.
Distinct recurrence in a mixed-image delivery: the first image opened, but the second was again inaccessible as JFIF.
Later regression in the terminal-study delivery: a new presentation image was again unviewable because it was JFIF.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

This is unquestionably the strongest option we’ve reached so far. The base no longer has a break, the right arm reads as one continuous structural form, and its perfectly straight inner edge finally causes the negative space to appear as a passive outcome rather than the central design goal. I believe you’re now approaching the challenge in the correct way.

Even so, it has not yet reached the degree of elegance I’m seeking.

The right arm remains overly bulky and visually weighty. I’m not looking for a clunky V or a "hero" right arm; I’m looking for an elegant V. At the moment, the right arm still attracts my attention before I can perceive the letter as a unified whole.

I don’t believe the answer is to make the right arm dramatically unlike the left. Instead, it needs greater refinement. Its strength should come through restraint, proportion, and precision rather than sheer mass. The asymmetry should register as sophisticated, not conspicuous.

We are also reaching a stage where the interaction between the two arms matters as much as the right arm in isolation. Please begin examining their connection at the vertex and how they can operate together as a single harmonious form with intentional asymmetry.

My ultimate aim is not to design a remarkable right arm. It is to design a remarkable V. The asymmetry must support the harmony of the full letter rather than becoming the defining feature by itself.

The right arm is not supposed to call attention to itself. The complete V should be resolved so harmoniously that its asymmetry feels entirely natural.

I’m looking forward to the direction this next refinement takes.

execution.observed_behavior: The client successfully viewed and assessed detailed visual properties of the replacement review image.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
This newest round feels like a significant move forward. I don’t believe we’ve reached the final V, but the thinking seems to be getting closer to the right place.

The Dynamic Arch drew my attention, not because I’m asking for a curved left arm, but because it brings in something that hasn’t appeared before: grace and movement. This is the first time the arms have felt different not only in structure, but also in character.

I’d love to push that idea further while reversing the relationship: the left arm would stay quiet and grounded, while the right arm would introduce movement without becoming decorative.

The right arm shouldn’t seem heavier merely because it is thicker. Its difference should come from its expression: elegant, quietly expressive, intentional, and sculptural. It should be something the viewer appreciates only after first taking in the V as a complete letter.

This also feels like the appropriate moment to develop the vertex and right arm together instead of approaching them as independent issues. Their relationship will ultimately determine the letter’s personality.

I no longer think we’re polishing one established concept; I believe we’re still exploring. Before narrowing toward a final form, I’d like to see several additional directions that are meaningfully distinct.

execution.observed_behavior: The client successfully viewed and evaluated the newly resent design round after the inaccessible second-image report.
